title: A Taxonomy of Runtime Faults in Model Context Protocol Servers
authors: Joshua Owotogbe, Indika Kumara, Antonio Ken Iannillo, Willem-Jan van den Heuvel, Damian Andrew Tamburri, Roberto Natella
central_claim: 833 confirmed MCP runtime-fault threads mined from GitHub issues/PRs of 473 maintained servers (funnel 78,267 issues + 49,155 PRs -> 4,649 fault-related -> 2,016 MCP-keyword -> 833); servers return well-formed success responses despite incorrect behavior.
cite_claim: Prior MCP fault mining is taxonomic: it classifies 833 issue threads but neither reproduces nor repairs any bug [C3]; its Threats section reports an 80% false-positive rate in a pilot of fault identification [verify exact scope in Sec. 7].
location: Sec. 4.1-4.5 (selection, funnel); Sec. 5.5 Tool Result Propagation; Sec. 6 Discussion; Sec. 7 Threats; Data Availability (figshare)
quote: The final dataset comprised 833 confirmed runtime fault threads used for taxonomy construction.
relevance: Reuse C3/C4. Our candidate set is the reproducible, repair-oriented complement; their replication package (https://figshare.com/s/c1e1e802e1b9f38fddf0) could seed more candidates. Note: data collected Sep 2025; no bug was reproduced (Sec. 6 proposes fault injection only).

title: Model Context Protocol (MCP) at First Glance: Studying the Security and Maintainability of MCP Servers
authors: Mohammed Mehedi Hasan, Hao Li, Emad Fallahzadeh, Gopi Krishnan Rajbahadur, Bram Adams, Ahmed E. Hassan
central_claim: Static analysis of 1,899 open-source MCP servers: 66% code smells, 14.4% contain ten bug patterns, 7.2% general vulnerabilities, 5.5% tool poisoning.
cite_claim: Static analysis flags bug patterns in 14.4% of 1,899 MCP servers [C5], but static patterns do not reveal behavioral, data-dependent silent faults such as unfollowed pagination tokens.
quote: while 66% exhibit code smells, 14.4% contain ten bug patterns overlapping prior research.
relevance: Reuse C5. Static-analysis baseline framing: a static-scanner baseline would be run over our real-bug prefixes to measure how many it flags.

title: Silent Bugs in Deep Learning Frameworks: An Empirical Study of Keras and TensorFlow
authors: Florian Tambon, Amin Nikanjam, Le An, Foutse Khomh, Giuliano Antoniol
central_claim: Defines silent bugs as wrong behavior without crash, hang, or error message; mined 1,168 closed Keras issues and found 77 reproducible silent bugs.
cite_claim: We adopt the established definition of a silent bug: wrong behavior without a crash, hang, or error message (Tambon et al.).
quote: lead to wrong behavior but they do not cause system crashes or hangs, nor show an error message to the user
relevance: Definition anchor and methodological precedent: mining issues for silent bugs, then filtering to the reproducible subset (77/1,168).

title: Gray Failure: The Achilles' Heel of Cloud-Scale Systems
authors: Ryan Huang, Chuanxiong Guo, Lidong Zhou, Jay Lorch, Yingnong Dang, Murali Chintalapati, Randolph Yao
central_claim: Cloud incidents are often caused by subtle gray failures rather than fail-stop failures; observers disagree on health.
cite_claim: Silent tool failures are an instance of gray failure: the server looks healthy to its own checks while the consumer observes wrong behavior.
quote: subtle underlying faults, i.e., gray failure rather than fail-stop failure
relevance: Systems lineage for 'differential observability' framing (C3 also cites it). [verify] full-text definition before quoting more.

title: GitBug-Java: A Reproducible Benchmark of Recent Java Bugs
authors: André Silva, Nuno Saavedra, Martin Monperrus
central_claim: 199 bugs from 55 repos (2023 history); each bug-fix runs 55 times offline in a Docker snapshot and only identical-result bugs are kept; funnel 508 candidates -> 199.
cite_claim: Following GitBug-Java, a real bug enters our benchmark only if its fail-before/pass-after result is identical across repeated offline executions.
location: Sec. 2.2 (fail/pass patterns), Sec. 2.3 (offline Docker snapshot), Sec. 2.4 (55 offline runs), funnel
quote: The bug-fixes that yield the exact same test results across all 55 executions are kept.
relevance: Methodology to copy for our real-bug harness: offline replay + N-run flakiness filter + recency to limit contamination. Their 508->199 attrition (39%) suggests budgeting for heavy loss.

title: BugSwarm: Mining and Continuously Growing a Dataset of Reproducible Failures and Fixes
authors: David A. Tomassi, Naji Dmeiri, Yichen Wang, Antara Bhowmick, Yen-Chuan Liu, Premkumar Devanbu, Bogdan Vasilescu, Cindy Rubio-González
central_claim: Automatically mines CI fail-pass pairs into reproducible containers; 3,091 Java/Python pairs.
cite_claim: Automated mining of reproducible fail-pass pairs at scale is established (BugSwarm), but CI fail-pass pairs are not the same as bug fixes.
quote: gathered 3,091 fail-pass pairs, in Java and Python
relevance: Pairs with durieux2019critical as the cautionary tale.

title: Critical Review of BugSwarm for Fault Localization and Program Repair
central_claim: Only 112 of BugSwarm's 3,091 pairs (3.6%) are suitable for evaluating fault localization or program repair.
cite_claim: Mined fail-pass pairs need manual curation: only 3.6% of BugSwarm pairs suit repair evaluation, so we report our candidate-to-benchmark attrition explicitly.
quote: only 112/3,091 (3.6%) are suitable to evaluate techniques for automatic fault localization or program repair
relevance: Reviewer-proofing: justify manual curation of our 68 candidates and report attrition at each gate.

title: BugsInPy: A Database of Existing Bugs in Python Programs to Enable Controlled Testing and Debugging Studies
authors: Ratnadira Widyasari, Sheng Qin Sim, Camellia Lok, et al., David Lo, Eng Lieh Ouh
central_claim: 493 real bugs from 17 Python programs, in the style of Defects4J, each with a bug-exposing test.
cite_claim: Real-bug benchmarks in the Defects4J tradition pair each bug with a bug-exposing test (BugsInPy, Defects4J); no such benchmark exists for MCP servers.
quote: Each bug comes with a test suite that can expose the bug.
relevance: Format precedent for our real-bug harness entries (prefix sha, fix sha, exposing test).

title: Defects4J: A Database of Real Faults and an Experimental Infrastructure
authors: René Just, Darioush Jalali, Michael D. Ernst
central_claim: Canonical database of real faults with experimental infrastructure for controlled SE experiments.
cite_claim: Defects4J established the real-fault benchmark format our MCP real-bug set follows.
quote: A Database of Real Faults and an Experimental Infrastructure to Enable Controlled Experiments in Software Engineering Research
relevance: Format/lineage only. [verify] ISSTA paper metadata (authors/venue taken from common knowledge, repo verified).

title: Multi-SWE-bench: A Multilingual Benchmark for Issue Resolving
authors: Daoguang Zan, Zhirong Huang, Wei Liu, et al. (19 authors)
central_claim: 1,632 issue-resolving instances across Java, TS, JS, Go, Rust, C, C++, annotated from 2,456 candidates by 68 experts.
cite_claim: Issue-resolution benchmarks now span Go and TypeScript (Multi-SWE-bench), the main languages of the MCP servers in our candidate set.
quote: carefully annotated from 2,456 candidates by 68 expert annotators
relevance: Possible external repair benchmark for Go/TS repair-agent calibration; its instances are generic issues, not silent tool faults.

title: Model Context Protocol Specification 2025-11-25: Tools
central_claim: Tool execution errors (API failures, validation, business logic) are to be reported in results with isError: true; servers MUST conform to a declared outputSchema; clients SHOULD validate results.
cite_claim: The spec expects API failures to surface as isError tool results; every bug in cluster C (swallowed upstream error returned as an empty success) violates this expectation without violating any schema.
location: Error Handling; Output Schema; Security Considerations
quote: Tool Execution Errors: Reported in tool results with isError: true
relevance: Reuse key from mcp-market (and C26). Normative baseline against which 'silent' is defined.

title: filesystem: edit_file silently converts a CRLF file's line endings to LF (issue #4991) and Wave 1 characterization suite (#4854/#4857)
central_claim: Reference-server maintainers first pinned current behavior with characterization tests, marking known silent bugs as KNOWN BUG tests that assert the wrong behavior, then fixed them.
cite_claim: Even the MCP reference servers shipped silent data-changing bugs that maintainers first pinned as 'KNOWN BUG' characterization tests before fixing them.
location: #4991 body ('Where it is pinned'); tracker #4857 Wave 1; #4854 Goal
quote: Each of these tests carries a `KNOWN BUG` marker: it asserts the current, wrong behavior
relevance: Industry precedent for 'test that encodes the bug first' (fiks F gate). Fixed by merged PR #5011.

title: list_pull_request_reviews silently truncates results to first page (~30 items) with no pagination support
central_claim: Official GitHub MCP server returned only the first page of PR reviews with no pagination and no truncation signal; fixed by PR #2367.
cite_claim: Pagination truncation (fiks D4) occurs in the official GitHub MCP server: the tool returned only the first ~30 reviews with no signal.
quote: only returns the first page of results (~30 reviews) and provides no way to fetch subsequent pages
relevance: Real analogue of seeded D4; merged fix -> F->P reproducible from recorded REST responses.

title: github_issue_write silently drops labels when caller lacks AddLabelsToLabelable permission
central_claim: issue_write returns success but applies no labels when the caller lacks permission; only a readback reveals it. Fixed by PR #3195.
cite_claim: A write that returns success but is not applied (fiks D3) occurred in the official GitHub MCP server and was detectable only by reading the issue back.
quote: The failure is only detectable by reading back the issue's labels.
relevance: Direct real-world support for read-after-write postconditions.

title: jira_update_issue silently drops parent: null (clearing epic membership fails but returns success)
central_claim: Clearing a Jira parent was skipped while the tool reported success; fixed in PR #1518. Sibling open reports: #1189 (components), #1578 (epic link).
cite_claim: Lost writes reported as success recur in the most popular community Atlassian MCP server (#1500, #1189, #1578).
quote: the tool still returns a success response — so callers cannot tell the write failed.
relevance: Python + HTTP upstream; three related candidates, two still open (fork-only fiks repair targets).

title: Workers Observability: required outcome field discards entire response (46% of real events, 86% of cron)
central_claim: A strict response schema (.parse over the whole array) made one missing field discard all events, so the tool returned no logs; fixed by PR #517.
cite_claim: Over-strict schema validation inside a server can itself cause a silent empty result: one event without an optional-in-practice field discarded the entire response.
quote: a single event without `outcome` throws away the **entire** response — the tool returns no logs at all.
relevance: Counter-evidence to 'more schema validation = safer'; argues for semantic invariants (non-empty for known-good input) rather than stricter schemas.

title: get_fields/search_fields return [] on connection failure, indistinguishable from 'no match'
central_claim: A catch-all returns an empty list on connection failure; same pattern in #1736 (401 -> empty dev info).
cite_claim: Swallowed upstream errors turned into empty successes are a recurring pattern (mcp-atlassian #1652, #1736; filesystem #5189; Azure Backup #3840).
quote: The empty list is a swallowed connection error, not a "no results" answer.
relevance: Cluster C exemplar; raw upstream HTTP in the fiks trace exposes the error directly.

title: (aws-network-mcp-server): get_all_tgw_routes route table pagination never passes NextToken
central_claim: Pagination loop re-requests page 1 because NextToken is never forwarded; sibling bugs in ECS (#4719/#4720), Step Functions (#2050), HealthOmics (#4639).
cite_claim: Unfollowed pagination tokens recur across AWS's official MCP servers (aws-network, ECS, Step Functions, HealthOmics).
quote: it never passes the `NextToken` it checks, so every call asks for the first page again.
relevance: Python/boto3: botocore Stubber gives deterministic offline fixtures; strong real-bug D4 cluster.

title: fix(billing-cost-management-mcp-server): verify empty cost-explore results before reporting $0
central_claim: Wrong Cost Explorer filter values return no rows, indistinguishable from a real zero, so the agent reports $0 for existing spend; fix adds verification guidance.
cite_claim: Silent empties produce confidently wrong numeric answers: an AWS cost tool led agents to report $0 for spend that existed.
quote: returns no rows, which is indistinguishable from a genuine zero, so the agent reports $0 for spend that exists.
relevance: Shows that some maintainers 'fix' silent failures in the tool description, not the code: a repair-target ambiguity reviewers will raise.

title: generate_deeplink: ISO 8601 timestamps in timeRange produce wrong time in Grafana UI
central_claim: ISO-8601 timestamps without milliseconds are misparsed by Grafana's URL parser, yielding the wrong time window; fixed by PR #808.
cite_claim: Timestamp-format faults (fiks D5) occur in the official Grafana MCP server.
quote: the generated URL produces the wrong time range in Grafana's UI.
relevance: Real D5 analogue; pure function, trivially offline.

title: add_dashboard_element: only the first dashboard filter binds when several are requested for one tile
central_claim: Looker accepts the request with 200 but keeps only the first filterable; tool reports success; open, with exact source lines cited.
cite_claim: Partial writes accepted with HTTP 200 occur in Google's MCP Toolbox (Looker add_dashboard_element).
quote: No error is returned: the API answers 200 and the element is created
relevance: Open bug with pinned source lines and SHA ff82869: ideal fork-only fiks target.

title: fix: incorrect number of clusters found (PR #561)
central_claim: The tool reported 'Found N clusters' using the length of a joined string, not the number of clusters.
cite_claim: Wrong-count bugs are small and common: MongoDB's MCP server reported a string length as the cluster count.
quote: Found ${rows.length} clusters in project
relevance: Minimal-diff real bug; good sanity case for repair agent and count==rows invariant.

title: create_or_update_file silently truncates large files (~500+ lines)
central_claim: A detailed user report of silent truncation was closed after maintainers could not reproduce it.
cite_claim: Not every reported silent failure is real: a detailed truncation report against the GitHub MCP server could not be reproduced by maintainers.
quote: Could not reproduce, there is nothing in our codebase that would do this
relevance: Negative control for false-positive analysis and for the F gate (fiks should fail to produce a failing repro).

title: Sift: Reliability gateway for AI tool output
central_claim: An MCP/CLI gateway that stores full tool output as artifacts and enforces pagination completion signals without changing upstream servers.
cite_claim: Runtime gateways can mitigate partial-data answers (Sift enforces pagination completion), but cannot fix a server that never forwards the upstream cursor.
quote: Upstream API pagination often sits outside MCP list-cursor flows, so agents can stop early and answer on partial data.
relevance: Runnable detection/mitigation-only baseline (MIT). Its author promoted it on awslabs/mcp#2050 as a workaround for a pagination bug: the 'monitor instead of fix' position in the wild.

title: Bug: list_runs returns empty response {"data":{"type":""}} due to jsonapi marshaling issue
central_claim: list_runs returned an empty JSON:API object for every query; fixed by PR #275; a later bug (#531) silently ignored the status filter.
cite_claim: Official vendor MCP servers have shipped tools that returned empty data for every input (HashiCorp list_runs).
quote: The `list_runs` tool returns an empty response `{"data":{"type":""}}` for all query patterns
relevance: MPL-2.0 (file-level copyleft; fork patches must stay MPL).

title: memory: create_entities silently drops observations for existing entities
central_claim: The reference memory server ignored entities that already existed, dropping new facts while reporting only created entities; fixed by PR #5008.
cite_claim: The MCP reference memory server silently dropped writes for existing entities.
quote: the fact is dropped with no indication.
relevance: Local (no HTTP) lost write: tests whether fiks contracts generalise beyond HTTP-wrapping servers.
